title: burst-credit-reconciler-rollback-and-customer-fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers experienced sudden capacity denials for burst traffic when a reconciler job rolled back an in-flight burst-credit ledger update after a routine deployment. Symptoms: reserved pool tenants observed sustained 429/503 errors for ~11-18 minutes, followed by burst credit resynchronization and gradual recovery. Impact: production latency spikes and failed requests for 6 enterprise Dedicated tenants (notably Finly, MedAtlas). This ticket tracks the hotfix, root-cause analysis, and permanent remediation plan.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy autoscaler reconciler v2.4.1 to staging with simulated burst credit drift
2) Trigger synthetic bursts from 10 tenants simultaneously to drive ledger updates
3) At the same time, induce a reconciler process restart to cause partial checkpoint writeback
4) Observe reconciler rollback path: stale TTL entries cause double-apply suppression, leaving tenants with zero visible burst credits
5) Verify that requests to reserved pools receive rejection due to perceived insufficient burst balance

mitigation: Immediate: rollback reconciler service to v2.4.0 (pre-deploy state) across affected regions
Short-term: run ledger-repair safe-reapply for tenants with negative or missing burst balances
Operational: increase reconciler leader election timeouts to avoid mid-write leadership flips during heavy bursts
Customer comms: notify affected customers with timeline, apologies, and action items (status page + targeted emails)
root_cause: A race between reconciler checkpoint trimming and a concurrent rollback path left some tenant ledger entries in a partially-applied state. The reconciler's rollback logic suppressed re-apply attempts when TTLs appeared stale, which in the presence of rapid bursts resulted in zeroing a tenant's visible burst-credit window. Two contributing factors: 1) non-idempotent ledger write semantics in the reconciler; 2) leader handoff occurring before in-memory commit confirmation was propagated to storage replicas.
fix_plan: 1) Make reconciler ledger updates idempotent: include monotonic op-sequence token and write-if-higher semantics
2) Implement deterministic checkpoint commit protocol: only mark checkpoint complete after storage ACKs from quorum
3) Add a guarded reconciliation safety window that rejects rollback if an overlapping burst is in flight
4) Deploy fix to a single region canary, monitor key metrics (reserved-pool rejection rate, burst ledgers inconsistencies), then ramp
5) Add end-to-end e2e test that simulates reconciler restarts during heavy bursts
qa_steps: Create synthetic load harness that reproduces the race at high probability
Run reconciler restart stress tests across multiple instance leaders and verify ledger invariants
Inject chaos (leader flaps) during checkpoint commit in staging and assert no tenant loses burst visibility
Verify rollback path no longer suppresses safe reapply under TTL skew
Smoke test with 10 enterprise tenants under realistic burst patterns for 24h before production rollout
rollout_plan: Canary rollout to us-west-2 (5% of reserved pool traffic) for 3 hours with automated guardrails. If no regression, progressively increase to 25% then 100% over 48 hours. Emergency abort triggers: reserved-pool rejection rate > baseline + 2% sustained for 10 minutes or any customer-reported 429 spike affecting SLA-tiered tenants.
